content: The document outlines a surveillance project aimed at assessing the prevalence of hepatitis B (HBV), hepatitis C (HCV), and hepatitis D (HDV) infections in patients with chronic liver disease, including those undergoing liver transplantation. The project involves reviewing medical records and existing blood test results to identify potential causes of chronic liver disease. No additional tests will be conducted, and the data collected will be anonymized to protect patient identity. The surveillance activity does not require any additional time or effort from patients and poses no risk to them. It solely involves the analysis of existing medical records, particularly focusing on test results for hepatitis B, C, and D. Patients will not receive any payment or compensation for their participation, as it does not involve active engagement. However, they retain the right to refuse the use of their data. If a patient opts out, their data will be destroyed and excluded from the project, without any impact on the care they receive at the clinical center. The project aims to provide valuable insights into the prevalence of viral hepatitis in patients with chronic liver disease, which could help the Ministry of Health improve healthcare planning and responses to hepatitis. Patients are encouraged to contact the designated person in charge of the surveillance activity or the institution for any questions or concerns about the project or its ethical aspects.
